claims.text: hippo-memory stores agent memories in SQLite, tracks provenance and lets feedback suppress incorrect memories.

evidence.quote: A memory layer for AI agents. Mark a memory wrong and it stops coming back. A newer fact replaces the old one. Memories you use get stronger. Provenance on every memory. SQLite under the hood, zero runtime deps, works with every CLI agent you have.

Hippo learns from outcomes. When a recalled memory turns out wrong, mark it bad and it drops out of the top results. Memories you keep using get stronger. Those two are the parts we measured helping ([mechanism audit, round 2](https://github.com/kitfunso/hippo-memory/pull/232)). When a fact changes, the new version supersedes the old one; we have not measured whether that helps. The design borrows from the hippocampus (decay, three layers, sleep consolidation), but that is inspiration. We have not measured decay or sleep making recall better.

It also fixes the portability problem. Your ChatGPT memories don't travel to Claude. Your `.cursorrules` don't travel to Codex. Hippo is one process behind every agent. CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules, ChatGPT exports, Slack history, all in one SQLite store, all queryable from any tool that speaks MCP or HTTP.

claims.text: Its optional Jev reranker orders recalled memories and is disabled by default.

evidence.quote: - **R@1 0.41 to 0.62 with `hippo recall "<query>" --reranker jev`** on a private 300-query developer store ([full eval](docs/evals/2026-09-19-jev-reranker.md)). The opt-in [TypeSafe Jev](https://typesafe.ai) reranker, off by default, about 0.0004 USD a recall. 2000-draw paired bootstrap; the margin held in 20 of 20 seeds and a permutation null reached it in 0 of 200 runs. Ranking only: three graded tests did **not** show a better answer rate than the free local cross-encoder, and that negative result is in the same doc. What it buys today is a shorter context, 2 memories ranked by Jev answering as well as 5 ranked by the cross-encoder.

claims.text: Agents can remember and recall through the CLI or MCP, sharing memory across coding tools.

evidence.quote:
```bash
# Manual usage
hippo remember "FRED cache silently dropped the tips_10y series" --tag error
hippo recall "data pipeline issues" --budget 2000
```

```
Works with:    Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Pi, any MCP client
Imports from:  ChatGPT, Claude (CLAUDE.md), Cursor (.cursorrules), Slack, markdown
Storage:       SQLite backbone with markdown mirrors. Git-trackable, human-readable.
Dependencies:  Zero runtime deps. Node.js 22.16+. Optional embeddings: bring-your-own local Transformers.js (`npm i @huggingface/transformers`, or legacy `@xenova/transformers`) or an opt-in API embedder (OpenAI/Voyage/Cohere). Nothing is auto-installed.

claims.text: Provider features can send memory text outside the machine; published retrieval results do not yet prove better agent task performance.

evidence.quote: On your machine, in SQLite: `.hippo/hippo.db` in each project, plus a global store in `~/.hippo/` for lessons shared across projects, with markdown mirrors you can read and commit. Recall makes no network call by default. Text goes to an outside provider only through features that use one: an API embedder, the Jev or LLM reranker, `hippo refine`, and the fact extraction `hippo sleep` runs through Anthropic's API whenever `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set in its environment. To turn that last one off, set `{"extraction":{"enabled":false}}` in `.hippo/config.json`.

### Has hippo been shown to make agents better at their work?

Not yet. The published numbers measure retrieval: whether the right memory comes back, and whether a memory marked wrong stays out of the results. A paired test that runs real agent sessions with and without hippo is under way. Every measurement, including failed runs and one retracted claim, is indexed in [docs/evals](https://github.com/kitfunso/hippo-memory/blob/master/docs/evals/README.md).

tr.summary: hippo-memory ajan anılarını SQLite’ta saklar, kaynağını izler ve geri bildirimle yanlış anıları bastırır. İsteğe bağlı Jev yeniden sıralayıcısı bulunan anıları sıralar; varsayılan olarak kapalıdır. Ajanlar CLI veya MCP üzerinden anıları kaydedip çağırarak kodlama araçları arasında paylaşabilir.

sections.heading: Ne işe yarar
sections.text: hippo-memory ajan anılarını SQLite’ta saklar, kaynağını izler ve geri bildirimle yanlış anıları bastırır.

sections.heading: Jev’in rolü
sections.text: İsteğe bağlı Jev yeniden sıralayıcısı bulunan anıları sıralar; varsayılan olarak kapalıdır.

sections.heading: Kullanım
sections.text: Ajanlar CLI veya MCP üzerinden anıları kaydedip çağırarak kodlama araçları arasında paylaşabilir.

sections.heading: Sınırlamalar
sections.text: Sağlayıcı özellikleri bellek metnini makine dışına gönderebilir; yayımlanan erişim sonuçları henüz daha iyi ajan görev başarısını kanıtlamaz.

it.title: hippo-memory: memoria con riordino Jev facoltativo
it.h1: hippo-memory: memoria con riordino Jev facoltativo
it.description: hippo-memory conserva e corregge ricordi in SQLite. Il riordinatore Jev facoltativo ordina i passaggi recuperati ed è disattivato di default.
it.summary: hippo-memory conserva ricordi in SQLite, ne traccia l’origine e sopprime quelli errati in base al feedback. Il riordinatore Jev facoltativo ordina i ricordi recuperati ed è disattivato per impostazione predefinita. Gli agenti memorizzano e richiamano informazioni tramite CLI o MCP, condividendole fra strumenti di programmazione.

sections.heading: A cosa serve
sections.text: hippo-memory conserva ricordi in SQLite, ne traccia l’origine e sopprime quelli errati in base al feedback.

sections.heading: Il ruolo di Jev
sections.text: Il riordinatore Jev facoltativo ordina i ricordi recuperati ed è disattivato per impostazione predefinita.

sections.heading: Come usarlo
sections.text: Gli agenti memorizzano e richiamano informazioni tramite CLI o MCP, condividendole fra strumenti di programmazione.

sections.heading: Limiti
sections.text: Alcune funzioni inviano testo a fornitori esterni; i risultati di recupero non dimostrano ancora migliori prestazioni degli agenti nei compiti.
